newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Cyclone swirls towards S.Africa from Madagascar.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone swirls towards S.Africa from Madagascar.

text.p: A cyclone which has wreaked havoc in Madagascar is heading towards Mozambique and South Africa, prompting forecasters to issue warnings of heavy rains, gale-force winds and high seas along the Indian Ocean coast.
Cyclone Gretelle is, however, not expected to cause serious damage in South Africa's northern-eastern coast in the KwaZulu-Natal region nor in neighbouring Mozambique.

"There are warnings out for heavy rain, meaning more than 50mm in a 24-hour period, also gale-force winds and very high seas off the coast of southern Mozambique and northern KwaZulu -Natal," Pretoria's chief forecaster Mike Edwards told Reuters.
"As the storm centre is not expected to move inland, we are not at this stage forecasting devastating rain."

Edwards said the centre of the storm was out over the Indian Ocean about 400 km (250 miles) east of Mozambique's capital Maputo on Monday afternoon, heading west from Madagascar, and was not expected to move much in the next 36 to 48 hours.

"On January 31, it is expected to weaken appreciably and then to gradually start moving away. But we are watching it very, very closely on satellite imagery and on lightning strike equipment," Edwards added.

On average, cyclones reach South Africa's seas only once every five years. Although one came in over Mozambique's northern coast last year, Edwards said a cyclone last hit the South African coast about 10 years ago.

Cyclone Gretelle has reportedly left more than 30,000 people homeless and more than 100 dead or missing in Madagascar, the world's fourth largest island, and has been labelled the worst there in living memory.
